Solid, mostly mechanical cleanup: centralising the per-service spec mocks in `create_services_mock()` removes a lot of duplicated `services_mock.X = Mock(XService)` boilerplate, and retyping the fixture as `Mock` is correct (it never was a `ServiceCollectionV3`).

Three things worth addressing before merge:

1. **Dead mock setup in `test_machines.py`** (`endpoints_with_authentication_only`, lines 213-215). `ApiCommonTests.test_endpoints_require_authentication_only` calls `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()`, which reassigns `services_mock.openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value = AsyncOpenFGAClientMock(set())` *after* the fixture ran, so the `list_pools_*` return values are discarded. `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__getattr__` then returns `False` for those calls and `machines.py:122` does `set(view_access_pools)` → `TypeError` → 500. The test only passes because it asserts `status_code not in (401, 403)`. Configure pool access through `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` instead.

2. **Behavioural trade-off of always-populated services**: previously `Mock(ServiceCollectionV3)` raised `AttributeError` for any service a test had not explicitly mocked, which failed loudly when a handler touched an unexpected dependency. Now every service resolves to a `Mock`, so a handler can call an unconfigured service and the test still passes on a `MagicMock`. This change already shows the effect — `test_ipranges.py:77` and `test_resource_pools.py` had to pin `get_one`/`get_by_id` to `None` to stop the authz tests flipping from 500 to 403. The trade-off is reasonable, but it is a real loss of strictness and deserves a note in the commit body.

3. **Description/diff mismatch**: the description says `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` is improved "to make it possible to pass pool permissions", but `src/tests/maasapiserver/fixtures/app.py` contains no such change — only the type-hint edits and the removal of the local `openfga_tuples` mock. Either land that improvement (it is what item 1 needs) or drop the claim.

No security concerns; this is test-only code and no credentials/inputs are involved.

src/tests/fixtures/__init__.py.66:
Two robustness/perf notes:

- `ServiceCollectionV3.__annotations__` returns raw annotation objects today, but it silently becomes `dict[str, str]` the moment anyone adds `from __future__ import annotations` to `maasservicelayer/services/__init__.py` (or on Python 3.14 defaults). Every service would then be specced on a `str`, breaking the whole suite with cryptic `AttributeError`s. `typing.get_type_hints(ServiceCollectionV3)` is the safe equivalent.
- A service added to `produce()` without a class-level annotation is silently absent here and fails with `AttributeError` on the specced parent — worth a short comment stating the annotation is the contract.
- [INFERENCE] this builds ~85 specced `Mock`s for every test that touches the fixture (plus each explicit `create_services_mock()` call); each `Mock(spec=cls)` walks `dir(cls)` and classifies async methods. Not a blocker, but if suite time regresses noticeably, lazy per-attribute creation (custom `__getattr__`) would avoid building the 84 mocks a test never uses.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.41:
The root cause is worth capturing more precisely than the comment does: `Mock(spec=Service)` makes async methods `AsyncMock`, and an `AsyncMock`'s `return_value` is itself an `AsyncMock` (`_get_child_mock` picks `AsyncMock` for `'()'`), so *any* method call on a service's return value produces an un-awaited coroutine.

That means this filter also masks a genuine missing `await` in handler code. Since these three tests only assert status codes they would not have caught it anyway, so suppression is acceptable — but the cleaner fix is in `create_services_mock()`: give async service methods a plain `MagicMock` return value, which removes the warning at source and lets all three `filterwarnings` markers (and the repeated "See the comment above") disappear.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.213:
These three lines have no effect. `test_endpoints_require_authentication_only` (base.py:94) calls `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions()`, which overwrites `services_mock.openfga_tuples.get_client.return_value` with `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock(set())` after this fixture has run. The handler therefore gets `False` (from `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock.__getattr__`) for both `list_pools_*` calls, and `machines.py:122` `set(view_access_pools)` raises `TypeError: 'bool' object is not iterable` → 500. The test still passes only because it asserts `status_code not in (401, 403)`, i.e. the endpoint is not actually exercised as intended.

Fix by making `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` able to return pool lists (the "pool permissions" improvement mentioned in the description) and configuring it through `mocked_api_client_user_with_permissions`, rather than on the soon-to-be-replaced `get_client.return_value`. `services_mock.machines.get_one.return_value = None` (line 216) is fine — that one is not clobbered.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/ha.77: A fixture named `endpoints_with_authentication_only` that also mutates `services_mock` is surprising: the base class documents it as "return a list of endpoints". The mock setup is only needed because `ipranges.get_one` now returns a `MagicMock` (ownership check → 403) instead of raising `AttributeError`. Consider making the intent explicit in the base class, e.g. an overridable `setup_mocks_for_authentication_only(services_mock)` hook called from the test, so the data fixture stays a data fixture.

src/tests/maasapiserver/v3/api/public/mo.296: While you are touching these blocks: `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock` is declared as `permissions: set[MAASResourceEntitlement] | None`, but it is being handed a bare `StrEnum` member. `self._permissions` then becomes the string `"can_edit_global_entities"` and every `in` check degrades to a substring test — both `has_permission_on_maas` and the `__getattr__` fallback (`item in self._permissions`, where `item` is a method name). It happens to return the right answer here, but it will produce silent false positives for any entitlement/method name that is a substring. Wrap in a set (`{MAASResourceEntitlement.CAN_EDIT_GLOBAL_ENTITIES}`, as `test_usergroups.py` does) or change the constructor to `*permissions`. Same applies to the `AsyncOpenFGAClientMock(None)` call above and the `_make_admin_services_mock` helper.
